out.other_title: MNIST debate with precommit: judge accuracy 59.4% to 88.9% (6 px), 48.2% to 85.2% (4 px)
out.rationale: Leike et al. describe Irving et al.'s MNIST experiments, in which the debating agents boost the accuracy of a sparse classifier that only has access to a few of the image's pixels, as promising initial experiments and say more research is needed; the passage does not dispute the reported accuracies.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: Leike et al.'s direct comment on Irving et al.'s MNIST debate experiments, in which debating agents boost a sparse classifier's accuracy, as promising initial results that need more research. Irving et al. report the boost (a 59.4% accurate judge becoming an 88.9% accurate debate with 6 pixels, and 48.2% becoming 85.2% with 4 pixels) for debate with precommit, which they call crucial because the liar does much better if the lie can adapt; Leike et al.'s summary does not mention precommit.

text: The authors summarize Irving et al.'s debate proposal and its central assumption that telling the truth is easier than lying, and describe the MNIST experiments, where debaters boost a sparse classifier's accuracy, as promising initial results. They add that more research on debate is needed.
title: Irving et al.'s MNIST debate results seen as promising, with more research needed
